lines.text: On a commercial flight, the passenger sitting directly next to you in economy might have paid half your ticket price.
Airlines pioneered dynamic yield management algorithms to squeeze maximum revenue from every single seat.
A flight's seats are divided into invisible pricing tiers called fare buckets.
Early leisure travelers book cheap bucket seats months ahead of time.
As departure day nears, remaining seats shift into corporate business buckets priced three times higher.
Algorithms update prices thousands of times a day based on route searches, fuel prices, and competitor inventory.
The best sweet spot for domestic flight prices is typically one to three months before takeoff.
